I liked the philosophy and politics of it. I'm a bit of an oddity where this movie is concerned. Most people who read the books are horrified by the movies, but to me it was sort of like the "cliffs notes" of the book - putting performances to the events I already knew about. It's incomplete, and somewhat flawed. I can definitely understand how people would be turned off. There are deeper themes going on in the show that many who didn't read the books simply won't be exposed to and the movie doesn't do a good job explaining.

I don't think I'd go as far as saying it was as bad as Battlefield: Earth, but it definitely wasn't the best Scifi ever made. I liked the atmosphere of it, and I felt that despite the stunted script that the acting was actually not bad. Keep in mind there are two versions of this movie - the first is the one most people know where a lot of the film was cut. The second is nearly a full hour longer (there is rumored to even be a 4 hour version but I've never seen it so I can't confirm if this is an urban legend) and explains more but is so cheesy in parts you can literally agree with the scene cutting.

Away from the movie, dune is a really amazing and complex concept as a scifi that deals with religion, biology, eugenics, politics, faction power struggles, and prophecy rooted in both science and mysticism that cinema still has yet to do proper justice to.
